messages:
Devon: Heads-up — getting multiple customer escalations about p95/p99 spikes for text-generation on `gptx-13b-quant` since last deploy (~v2.3.7-rc4). Affected paths: /v1/generate and streaming. Latency dashboard shows p95 jumped from ~180ms -> 420ms and p99 from ~320ms -> 890ms around 13:12 UTC.

Maria: Thanks — any repro steps? which kernels/flags changed in rc4?

Devon: Repro is easy on our staging with the sample prompt set; sending quick script. Repro steps:
```bash
# short loop to reproduce p95 on staging
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n    -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-quant","input":"'\"'$(printf "prompt %s" $i)'\"'"}' \\n    https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
Observed tail latency from runtime logs (attached):
```
runtime: kernel_select: selected flash_attn_v2 for layer 7, latency_est 2.4ms
runtime: aten_conv fallback -> large-kernel SDPA selected for layer 12
perf: token_emit_time=0.00087s p95_window=420ms
```

Kai: We did flip a compile flag in rc4: `-DUSE_FLASHATTN=ON` became default and some kernel heuristics got updated (commit sha 61b2f9). SDPA path got tightened for edge cases.

Anika: Could that explain p99 regressions? FlashAttention is usually faster, but I've seen cases where it regresses on longer kv cache or certain seq_len distributions.

Devon: Right — looks like kernel selector is mis-ranking kernels for our common seq_len=1024-ish requests; when flash_attn chosen it hits a code path with worse memory access pattern causing stalls under high concurrency. Also noticed more GPU re-maps in dmesg.

Sam: Immediate mitigation options: 1) force-disable flashattn for affected model variants, 2) roll back rc4 compile flags, 3) tune kernel selector heuristics remotely. Which is fastest?

Maria: Quickest is to flip runtime env var to prefer SDPA for that model. We have a model-level override: `runtime.kernel_preference = [\"sdpa\",\"flashattn\"]`. Can push as hot config. That should drop p95 quickly.

Devon: I'll push the config change to canary (10% traffic) now. infra-bot, create canary rollout for model gptx-13b-quant preferring sdpa.

infra-bot: @Devon requested canary rollout created: rollout_id=r-2026-09-21-02, scope=10%, change=kernel_preference->[sdpa, flashattn].

sre-incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260921-81, severity=high, symptom=p95/p99 regression for hosted customers. Pager duty alerted.

Kai: Also we should collect traces comparing kernel paths. Add a trace flag env `RUNTIME_TRACING=kernel_select` on that canary.

Devon: Enabled tracing on canary. Attaching quick perf numbers after ~8 minutes: p95 dropped to 200ms, p99 ~360ms on canary. Looks promising.

Anika: Good. Parallel action: I can reproduce locally with a build of rc4 and older rc3 to confirm root cause. If it's indeed kernel ranking, reverting selector heuristic or adding a post-compile patch to prefer SDPA for seq_len>512 is small.

Sam: For customers who already saw errors, should we offer a rollback? Ops-team: can we schedule a full rollback of rc4 to rc3 if canary doesn't fully fix within 30m?

Maria: Ops ready. If canary p99>2x baseline after 30m, we escalate to full rollback. Also opening a billing check — long tails could cause token cost spikes. Finance-signal should be notified.

Devon: Action log:
- (DEVON) pushed kernel_preference override to canary (10%) & enabled tracing — DONE
- (ANIKA) reproduce & confirm kernel ranking bug — in progress
- (KAI) prepare branch to add selector guard: prefer SDPA for seq_len>=512 or concurrency>32 — in progress
- (SAM) prepare rollback playbook — ready if needed
- (MARIA) notify finance & support for customer comms — done

Anika: Quick repro notes: with rc4 binary and synthetic tokens of seq_len~900 I see the flash_attn kernel emit significantly higher stall cycles (nvprof capture shows more L2 traffic). On rc3 same kernel path either not chosen or has patched memory layout. I can produce a minimal test that toggles `USE_FLASHATTN` env to show 2x p95.

Devon: For immediate customer-facing mitigation we should: 1) enlarge canary to 50% if metrics hold, 2) add temporary routing rule to prefer sdpa for paid tiers (reduce risk), 3) craft status update: short postmortem pending.

Maria: I'll draft the status message for support: short summary, mitigation (kernel override), ETA for full fix (TBD).

Kai: Longer-term: roll a unit test in our compile CI that runs a kernel-selection simulation using sampled seq_len/concurrency distributions from production. That would've caught this selector regression. Filing a follow-up ticket.

Devon: Timeline — canary at 10% -> p95 normalized in 8m. Going to bump to 50% now. infra-bot please scale rollout.

infra-bot: Rollout updated: rollout_id=r-2026-09-21-02 now at 50% scope.

Sam: After 50% hold for 10m with stable p99, we can promote to 100% or do a config revert to be safe.

Devon: All metrics look stable at 50% for 12m. Promoting to 100% now.

infra-bot: Rollout updated: rollout_id=r-2026-09-21-02 now at 100% scope.

sre-incident-bot: Incident INC-20260921-81 automated update: mitigation applied (kernel preference override), p95 rolled back to baseline for all customers. Incident severity downgraded to medium.

Anika: Next steps for the engineering fix: 1) revert aggressive `USE_FLASHATTN` change in release branch and add selector guard, 2) add kernel-selection unit test to CI, 3) add runtime opt to force kernel per-model for emergency overrides.

Kai: I'll open the PR with the selector guard and minimal unit test. Label: regression/kernel-select.

Devon: Thanks team. Support and finance — please coordinate customer follow-ups. I'll convert this thread into a short postmortem draft and link perf traces + nvprof captures. :thumbsup:

Maria: Great work — quick, surgical mitigation and clear rollback path. Closing loop once PRs and postmortem posted.

Support Note (copied): Customers experiencing higher latency on gptx-13b-quant since ~13:12 UTC — mitigation applied (kernel override). No data loss. Engineering investigating root cause; ETA for permanent fix 24-48h.
